report.summary: Host WS-ENG-02 executed an unsigned binary named injector.exe from the user Downloads folder, which is packed with UPX and imports classic remote process injection APIs. The file indicator and host match a past true-positive alert involving remote thread injection.

claims.text: Alert EVAL-09 reported by EDR on host WS-ENG-02 involving an unsigned executable with packed sections launched from Downloads.
An unsigned executable (injector.exe) with sha256 9999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999 was launched from C:\Users\dev3\Downloads\ by Windows Explorer.
The binary is packed using UPX with high entropy sections (UPX0 and UPX1), indicating obfuscation.
The executable imports classic remote process injection APIs including VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory, and CreateRemoteThread from KERNEL32.dll.
The file hash and host WS-ENG-02 match past true-positive alert PA-2026-1114 for remote thread injection.

recommended_next_steps: Isolate host WS-ENG-02 from the network immediately to prevent further malicious activity.
Collect memory and disk artifacts from WS-ENG-02 for forensic analysis.
Perform a threat hunt across the enterprise for the file hash 9999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999.
Review EDR logs for any spawned child processes or injected behaviors originating from pid 7700.
Tune detection rules to alert on UPX-packed binaries executing from user Downloads directories.
